paper.title: Online Learning to Rank with Features

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning to rank with features (factored general click model, linear attractiveness)
unmapped: Click probability factors as v(A,k)=chi(A,k)*alpha(A(k)) with unknown examination function chi
Attractiveness is linear in known item feature vectors: alpha(a)=<a,theta_*> in [0,1]
Examination function satisfies: depends only on the set of items above position k (Assumption 1), is decreasing in position (Assumption 2), and is minimal on the optimal ranking A* (Assumption 3)
Clicks across positions need not be conditionally independent
Regret measured relative to A* (items sorted by attractiveness), which need not maximize expected clicks
Learner knows the item feature vectors (finite item set of size L)
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t\in [T]$ the learner chooses a ranking $A_t \in \Sigma$ and subsequently receives feedback in the form of a vector $C_t \in \{0,1\}^K$ where $C_{tk} = 1$ if the user clicked on the $k$th position. ... $v(A, k) = \chi(A, k) \alpha(A(k))$ ... $\alpha(a) = \ip{a, \theta_{\ast}}$ for all $a \in \cL$.

symbols.m: number of positions in the ranking (paper's K)

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: There exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that the regret bound for Algorithm \ref{alg:main} with $\delta = 1/\sqrt{T}$ satisfies \begin{align*} R_T \le C K \sqrt{dT\log(LT)}\,. \end{align*}

results.notes: Paper's K (positions) mapped to m, paper's L (items) declared as L_items. Regret defined through expected click probabilities v, i.e. pseudo-regret relative to A*. Universal constant C hidden, so notation O. Running time polynomial: O(L d^2 log T + K d^2 T).
